name: Channel Profitability Divergence
description: One sales channel is quietly profitable while another is dragging down overall performance.
formula: Channel Profit = (Price - Variable Cost per Unit) × Units - Allocated Fixed Cost = Profit_A vs Profit_B
business_contexts: retailer comparing owned e-commerce against wholesale/distributor channel
consumer goods company comparing direct-to-consumer against big-box retail
hotel brand comparing direct bookings against third-party travel sites
insurer comparing independent agent sales against its direct call center
furniture company comparing showroom sales against online sales
question_patterns: Which channel is actually more profitable, and by how much?
What is the dollar profit gap between the two channels?
If the weaker channel matched the other channel's economics, how much more profit would the company earn?
How much of total profit is being dragged down by the weaker channel?
solution_logic: Step 1: Calculate Channel A profit = (channel_a_price - channel_a_variable_cost) × channel_a_units - channel_a_fixed_cost
Step 2: Calculate Channel B profit = (channel_b_price - channel_b_variable_cost) × channel_b_units - channel_b_fixed_cost
Step 3: Calculate profit gap = Channel A profit - Channel B profit
key_insight: Blended, company-wide margins can hide a channel that's actively destroying value — always break profitability down by channel before recommending a fix.
common_mistakes: Comparing channel revenue instead of channel profit
Treating the given fixed cost figures as needing further allocation instead of taking them as the channel's already-assigned cost
Assuming the higher-revenue channel is automatically the more profitable one
framework_soundbite: A healthy blended margin can hide one channel eating the other's lunch — split profit by channel before you diagnose.
